title: Leo Package Registry
description: Catalog of installable data-driven (no-rebuild) Leo packages.

name.description: Unique id. Used as a settings-key component, plugin URL segment, and MCP package name.

icon_url.description: Absolute https URL of this entry's artwork. The store-admin Worker ANNOTATES this at serve time and never stores it (services/store-admin/src/catalog.ts), so an entry copied from that catalog arrives carrying one. It is a real field here because the hub reads it — `RegistryEntry::icon_url` and `adopt_catalog_icon` fetch it once, materialize it into the hub's own icon ladder and never pass the third-party URL to a client. Absent is fine: the client draws the `icon` glyph instead. The `?v=` query is the artwork's `sha256[:16]`, which is what makes a changed icon re-adopt rather than sit cached.

shared.description: A shared runtime artifact (`leo-runtime`, `leo-duckdb`): installed only because another entry's artifact names it in `depends=`, never listed or offered as an app. A hub resolves each `.PKGINFO` `depend =` by pkgname against the hosted blocks of entries marked this way, so every byte it installs is hashed by the catalog and there is still no `depends` field on the wire (ruled 2026-11-16). Top-level rather than inside `hosted`, because it says what the ENTRY is, which a store reads before it reads how to install it. A shared entry's `name` is its pkgname.

name.description: The package's own name as its descriptor states it. Redundant with the entry's `name` and carried anyway: a `descriptor.json` published verbatim has it, and refusing the entry over a duplicated string would cost an install target to buy nothing.

details.description: The long-form description shown on the package's own page.

setup_hint.description: One paragraph telling the owner what to do before the package will work.

category.description: Mirrors `leo_sdk_decl::PackageCategory`, which is exactly these two.

host_api.description: The host API generation this package was built against.

oauth_provider.description: An OAuth provider (`google`) whose already-connected account the hub may hand this package a token for, instead of the package running a second consent flow of its own. Functional, not a hint: `McpMailProvider` and `McpCalendarProvider` are both constructed with it (leo-mcp/src/package.rs).

access.description: Who may reach this package, as `leo_sdk_decl::package_meta::Access` serialises it (`{"mode": "admin_only"}`). Shape deliberately NOT mirrored field-by-field here, for the reason the hosted block does not mirror the RESERVED name list: a third spelling of one fact is how the three come to disagree.

privileged_helper.description: A root-owned helper with a closed verb set, as `leo_sdk_decl::borrowed::PrivilegedHelper` serialises it. Shape not mirrored here, same reason as `access`.

ui.description: The package's UI tree. `Option<serde_json::Value>` in the hub, so any JSON — no constraint is honest here.

provides.description:
Subsystems this package's MCP server stands in for. Tools are what a package gives Claude; a provider is what it gives Leo — the wallpaper generator, the web_search tool and the speech pipeline each call one. The linked server must answer that role's tool: wallpaper -> search_photos, web_search -> search, tts -> synthesize (voices optional). Filling a role is shown at consent and is part of the install digest, so a role cannot be added after approval without the digest moving.

This enum IS `leo_mcp::providers::ProviderRole::ALL` and must stay equal to it. It said [wallpaper, web_search, tts] until 2026-11-17 while the hub had known nine roles for some time, and `mail`, `image_gen` and `calendar` are each published by a live catalog entry and wired to a real provider (leo-mcp/src/package.rs) — so the narrow list refused three working entries. Nothing in the Rust tree reads this file, so no guard catches the next such drift; widen it in the same commit that adds a variant.

entitlements.description: Capabilities the package needs, consented to at install. The broker grants exactly these — least privilege.

feed.description: May post to the user's feed.

settings_read.description: Settings keys (e.g. API keys) the package may read — and only these.

graph_scopes.description: Graph scopes the package's token carries (`people:read`, `satellites:operate`, …) — what `provision-host` mints beyond `settings:read`. Disclosed here because a hosted artifact declares them and § 5 of docs/package-store-distribution.md refuses an install whose artifact grants what the catalog never showed.

oauth_tokens.description: OAuth providers (`google`) whose USER tokens the package may be handed — permission to act as the user against a third party, not a connect-flow hint.

satellite_capabilities.description: Satellite capabilities (`browser`, `simulator`, …) the package may ask the hub to drive. `satellites:operate` in graph_scopes grants the verb; this bounds the subject.

network.description: Hostnames the package's process may reach.

sends.description: What classes of the owner's data leave the box, to which destination, and why — one entry per host. `network` says WHERE a package may dial; this says WHAT goes there, which is the half an owner actually needs to consent. A host in `network` with no entry here is reported at install as 'does NOT say what data it sends to …'.

inference.description: May ask Claude questions through the hub on the HOUSEHOLD's own credential (`POST /graph/v1/inference/messages`). A declaration of which classes of the owner's data go into prompts and why, not a flag: it is billed to the household's ceiling and ledger, which is the whole point of it being an entitlement rather than `anthropic_api_key` in `settings_read`. Joined the vocabulary 2026-11-16, when it was ruled to follow the hub's `Entitlements` type.

dataflow.description: One destination and what the package admits to sending it. A declaration naming no class, or no purpose, is a defect and is refused at install rather than shown as a disclosure.

classes.description: Coarse data classes (search_queries, prompts, conversations, mail, financial, …). Deliberately coarse: this is read at a consent prompt, not queried.

purpose.description: Why, in one plain sentence — the half a person actually reads, shown verbatim at consent. Named for the serialized field; `because()` is only the Rust builder's method name.

inference.description: The inference grant as the hub's `InferenceGrant` serialises it. Like a dataflow, one naming no class or no purpose is a defect and is refused at install rather than shown as a disclosure.

classes.description: Coarse data classes the package will put in prompts (prompts, conversations, mail, ...).

purpose.description: Why, in one plain sentence; shown verbatim at consent.

appspec.description:
App package: a standalone binary built from git on the host and run as a subprocess (NOT linked into Leo).

`additionalProperties` is true here, which is the one place in this schema that is so, and it is a measured decision rather than laziness. The hub's `AppSpec` has fields this block does not name (`supervised`, `socket`, `mounts`, `graph_routes`) and a real published entry — `spaces` — carries two the hub does not have AT ALL (`webapp`, `base_path`), which serde drops on the way in. Refusing the entry over a field nothing reads would cost an install target and buy no safety, since every field that grants anything lives in `descriptor.entitlements` and is still closed. Named fields keep their types; unknown ones pass.

rev.description: Pinned commit SHA. The hub fetches this exact commit and verifies the checkout against it, so the reviewed code is the built code.

branch.description: Fallback when `rev` is absent — a mutable reference the author can move after review. Deprecated for new entries.

build.description: Build command run in the clone (default: cargo build --release).

bin.description: Path to the built binary, relative to the clone root.

port.description: Fixed port, or 0 to assign a free one at spawn.

supervised.description: The init system owns this process: the hub neither fetches, builds nor spawns it, it adopts whatever answers on `socket`. How a first-party package hosted by `leo-package-host` presents itself.

socket.description: The Unix socket the app serves the package protocol on. Preferred over `port` — the kernel attests the peer.

options.description: Null is accepted because the hub's own type is `Option<Vec<String>>` and `serde_json` writes an unset one as `null`, so a descriptor serialised by the hub carries nulls here.

show_in_nav.description: Whether the page is listed in nav surfaces by default (`PageSpec::show_in_nav`, default true). Reachable via Cmd+K either way.

bundle.description: Frontend bundle. sha256 is REQUIRED for the public registry so a compromised host cannot inject JavaScript.

hosted.description: An OS package: one pacman artifact the hub downloads, verifies and installs with `pacman -U`, after which the package runs as its own systemd unit (leo-package@<name>) instead of linked into the hub. The fifth install surface and the heaviest - a root transaction placing a binary, a sysusers account and a D-Bus policy. Minimal on purpose: everything derivable is derived, because a field that can drift is a field that will. Four things an install needs are deliberately absent. The socket names: leo-package@.socket derives both from %i, and two spellings of one fact is how they disagree. libduckdb: the builder asks `ldd` of the binary and ships it or does not, so the loader follows the binary and a catalog field could contradict it. The unit templates: they belong to Leo OS (os/os-files.manifest) and are shared by every hosted package, and N packages owning one file is something pacman correctly refuses. The entitlements: reused from this entry's `descriptor.entitlements`, which is what the user was SHOWN - the artifact's own leo-package.json is the authority at install, and the two disagreeing is a refusal rather than a merge. Every key here is required: a half-written block is a publishing defect, and an install that filled one in would be installing something nobody declared.

pkgname.description: The pacman package name, always `leo-<name>` for this entry's own `name` - it was `leo-package-<name>` until the 2026-11-15 rename, and the PKGBUILD carries `replaces=('leo-package-<name>')`, so pacman retires the old name and the catalog never names it. Pinned to this grammar rather than taking any string because the `<name>` half becomes a systemd instance, a D-Bus name element, a unix account and a path before it is ever a package name, and each of those is narrower than a string. The install's own confinement on this route is exactly a character class - leo_core::package_service::validate, which every path-deriving function spends BEFORE the format! that joins the name, because refusing a name by class before it is ever joined is stronger than canonicalizing after the fact. The three assertions here are that same check: the class, no doubled hyphen, no trailing hyphen. `validate` also refuses a RESERVED list of names, which lives in Rust and is deliberately NOT mirrored here - a third spelling of that list is how it would come to disagree, and a reserved name is refused at install rather than being something a reviewer must memorise. Note what this does NOT claim: the `--overwrite` values of a takeover install are not derived from this name. Section 4 settles that they are package-independent constants, pinned in the sudoers rule with an escaped asterisk, with nothing to parameterise.

version.description: `pkgver-pkgrel`, pacman's spelling - not the package's own version string. A pacman pkgver may not contain a hyphen because that is the separator, so the builder rewrites `-` to `.` and appends the release: '0.4.0-1'. A bare '0.4.0' is not a pacman version and neither is '0.4.0-rc1'.

arch.description: The artifact's architecture as pacman spells it - 'x86_64', or 'any'. A pattern rather than an enum: refusing an architecture nobody has built for yet would be this file deciding something the builder owns, and a hub learns an arch mismatch from `pacman -U` refusing the file.

url.description: Where the artifact is. Named rather than computed from a template, so moving the host later is a catalog change and not a code change. Its basename should read `<pkgname>-<version>-<arch>.pkg.tar.zst`, and scripts/validate.py checks that the four agree - the sha256 pins the BYTES and not which package they are, so a url copied from a neighbouring entry verifies cleanly and installs something nobody reviewed.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the artifact, verified before pacman is handed the file. REQUIRED, for the reason bundle.sha256 is and a worse one: an unverified bundle is stored XSS, an unverified artifact is `pacman -U` as root. There is deliberately NO signature field - the hash arrives in the same JSON as the bytes it describes, so it catches a corrupted download and not a hostile catalog, and an optional signature nobody populates is worse than none because it reads as present. A real signature plus a required field is phase 2, when a key has a home.

size_bytes.description: The artifact's size. Lets a hub cap the download against the declared figure rather than only against a ceiling, and lets it say what it is about to fetch before fetching it - the hash cannot be checked until the last byte is already resident, so the size is the only bound available while reading.
